text: Emilio Marcos de Palma Morella (born 7 January 1978) is an Argentine man recognized as the first person born on the continent of Antarctica.[1][2] He was born at Fortín Sargento Cabral, located at Esperanza Base near the tip of the Antarctic Peninsula, and had a birth weight of 3.4 kg (7 lb 8 oz). His father, Captain Jorge Emilio Palma, served as the head of the Argentine Army detachment at the base.[3] Silvia Morella de Palma, who was seven months pregnant at the time, was airlifted to Esperanza Base in late 1977 to complete her pregnancy.[4] Emilio was born on 7 January 1978 and baptized at the Chapel of St. Francis of Assisi on the base.[5] He is listed in the Guinness Book of Records as the first person born on the continent.[6] This Argentine biographical article is a stub.
